fatal_errors: The proposed 15 Oe coercivity threshold does not establish improvement over the relevant FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives, whose coercivities may approach 100 Oe.
No specific almost-equiatomic multicomponent composition is given, so retention of the required high-entropy-alloy chemistry after the intervention is not demonstrated.
The requested supporting observations from earlier work are absent.
The intervention and mechanism miss the target Ti-induced fcc/C14 dual-phase microstructure and its interphase magnetic coupling.
explanation: Cryogenic milling and defect-mediated domain-wall pinning are generically plausible ways to increase coercivity, and the proposed measurements could test whether milling changes coercivity, grain size, and strain. However, the hypothesis does not reconstruct the FeCoNiTi intervention, rapid-quenched fcc/C14 coexistence, phase-specific magnetic transitions, antiferromagnetic sublattice coupling, or the approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K. Its assumed 10 Oe baseline and 15 Oe success criterion are unsupported and fail to guarantee superiority to the prior Pd/Pt alloys. The experiment also lacks an explicit unmilled composition-matched control and cannot distinguish defect pinning from contamination, phase transformation, or oxidation caused by milling.
